text:
noah: Quick flag: Avenue9b-int4 showing slow p99 and intermittent OOMs on longer sessions. Need pragmatic fixes before we dig deeper.

rae: Can you paste the workload? Long streaming or many short requests?

noah: Long streaming. Prompts ~900 tokens, then repeated generate of 150-200 tokens. p99 up ~2x after ~30m and then occasional cudaMalloc OOM.

mina: I ran a short experiment: disabling prefetch + lowering max_new_tokens from 400->200 stabilizes memory and brings p99 down ~35%. Throughput down ~10%.

eli: Sounds like KV allocation churn + int4 packing causing fragmentation. Two-prong: (A) quick config changes (prefetch=false, max_new_tokens=200, batch_max=2, slot_reserve=0.10), (B) short-term runtime flag to force int4_alignment=256 or 512.

noah: Let's canary A+B at 5% with mem_frag_ratio and p99 alerts. If stable, we roll conservatively.

mina: I also tried a background compaction pass every 10m (low priority) in the runtime; it reduced mem_frag_ratio by ~0.04 in our sim but needs canary testing.

sre-bot: canary-deploy: applying overrides to model=avenue9b-int4 audience=5% (flags: prefetch=false, max_new_tokens=200, batch_max=2, slot_reserve=0.10, int4_alignment=256)

rae: 30m in: p99 returned to within 10% of baseline, mem_frag_ratio stabilized at 0.03, no OOMs. Throughput impact ~9%.

eli: Recommendation: keep config overrides as model defaults, open PR for full int4 alignment and compaction behind feature flags. Add alert: mem_frag_ratio>0.12 or p99>baseline*1.25 -> rollback.

noah: Owners: eli PR alignment+compaction (48h), mina monitor canary + run 6h soak (6h), rae add dashboard alerts and dashboard panels (3h). If soak clean, rollout 10%->30%->100% over 36h.

mina: Will attach allocation histograms and QA delta table when soak finishes.

noah: Thanks team. This kept client SLAs intact.
